gen-megrim-gf-mitr: Megrim draws every stroke at a single measured thickness, giving its angular, futuristic letters a tall, skyward lift. Mitr is a friendly sans whose lowercase nearly reaches the capitals.
gen-megrim-gf-momo-trust-display: Megrim brings angular, futuristic letters whose strokes never swell or thin, each one ending at the same measured width. Momo Trust Display lets its spaced-out sans-serif letters drift beneath the sharp heading.
gen-megrim-gf-mukta-vaani: Megrim sketches angular, futuristic letters with plain constant-width lines and a lowercase line that stretches skyward. Mukta Vaani, a contemporary sans with a high-waisted lowercase, carries the text beneath.
gen-megrim-gf-narnoor: Angular and futuristic, yet drawn as if with a round-tipped pen. Megrim does its best work making a statement with that pen-drawn line, while Narnoor, plain sans with short ascenders over big bowls, handles the reading.
gen-megrim-gf-smooch-sans: Smooch Sans packs its sans-serif lines so closely that the gaps nearly vanish, though its s keeps generous openings. Give Megrim, with its shading-free strokes, plenty of size above it.
gen-megrim-gf-winky-rough: Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters with a marker-nib line that ignores direction. Winky Rough, a contemporary sans whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, makes paragraphs feel dense but steady.
gen-megrim-space-grotesk: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws each stroke to a single measured thickness, with a high lowercase line. Space Grotesk, a geometric sans with a moderate lowercase height, gives its open counters room at modest sizes.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-amulya: Amulya has a modern feel, with its curves left generously open. What stands out most is how the tall, open-jawed lowercase of Mystery Quest meets the moderate height of Amulya.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-plein: Plein reads clean and reliable, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. And beside the bookish, nostalgic Mystery Quest, this plain sans would carry paragraphs without tiring the eye.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-synonym: Mystery Quest cuts open jaws into every curved stroke. That bookish, nostalgic character is its best trick, while Synonym, a dependable sans-serif with generous curve openings, simply holds the text steady.
